items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: And shortly after that, Freddie Green joined and that was fantastic. It really made that group.

ctx.x: It started out Clark Terry and Bobby Graf from St. Louis, a tenor player, myself on front line, Bill Basie and Jimmy Lewis played bass and Gus Johnson played drums. And shortly after that, Freddie Green joined and that was fantastic. It really made that group.
You had to have Freddie, right?

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And he liked the group so much he had said to Basie, “I’m joining the band.” So he did

ctx.x: He essentially was the sound, or a lot of the sound of the rhythm section. And he liked the group so much he had said to Basie, “I’m joining the band.” So he did, “Yeah, great!” You know, and he came on, there again, he made such a difference too in the feel and the rhythm.

You, when you talk about the feel and the rhythm, was that a different experience for you in playing with all these musicians out of Kansas City, everybody talks about that Kansas City swing with the Basie band.
